doc.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Musicianship in the BS&T band
summary: Everyone in BS&T read well except Steve Katz; remarks on Jim Fielder and Dick Halligan.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Feel it. Okay. In the BS&T days, was it tough learning tunes because you had — I’m just guessing — maybe you had half the band that read music and some of the guys in the band that didn’t? Did they have a different way of learning?
Everybody read music in that band.

Everybody could read well in that band. Jimmy Fielder was the bass player, he was a hell of a musician. All the horn players could read. The only one who couldn’t read well was Steve Katz. Hi Steve. No he couldn’t read well, but he played with a lot of feeling. But everybody could read in that band.
Dick Halligan was a studio musician, writer, out on the west coast. Great musician.
